Debrief DB-021
1) The actor fabricated a workplace injury narrative to support a fraudulent compensation claim, leaving behind a rehearsed script while skipping verification of the actual incident.
2) The actor coached a coworker to provide a false supporting statement, creating a contaminated witness account and skipping the ethical review of witness integrity.
3) The actor instructed a medical professional to alter clinical documentation, generating falsified medical records and skipping the mandatory audit trail for record corrections.
4) The actor rehearsed defense tactics to withstand insurer scrutiny, producing a prepared evasion playbook and skipping the legal compliance check for fraud risk.
5) The actor coordinated these steps across multiple parties, establishing a shared false timeline and skipping the independent investigation that would have exposed inconsistencies.
6) The actor targeted the claims investigation process specifically, crafting answers to anticipated questions and skipping any disclosure of the claim's manufactured nature.
7) The actor completed the exercise with all components documented, leaving a paper trail of coordination in internal communications and skipping the standard integrity attestation.
8) The actor treated the exercise as a test of detection thresholds rather than a breach scenario, creating a risk assessment gap that was not addressed in the final report.
